properties.name: 5 National Park Hikes That Tested My Limit
properties.title: 5 National Park Hikes That Tested My Limit
properties.creator: @amorywild
properties.theme: 5 National Park Hikes That Tested My Limit
properties.recommendation_summary: Ranked #5, an 8-mile round trip with about 4,500 feet of gain, mostly off-trail on the second half. He stopped short of the summit in snow but had views of Lake McDonald. Ranked #4, a 10.5-mile round trip wading the Virgin River in cold water. He went in June during snowmelt and used a dry bib wetsuit. Ranked #3, described as logistically easy but hard because of high, cold water crossings that left him constantly off-balance, wearing wetsuit overalls and layers. Ranked #2, a 17-mile route with about 4,500 feet of gain done in June with snow at the top, which he calls one of the most beautiful hikes he has done despite loose rock. Ranked #1, an 8-mile hike with about 4,500 feet of gain and turquoise lake views. He says he was unprepared on his first attempt and later returned better prepared.

Channel Islands mini guide
properties.title: Channel Islands mini guide
properties.creator: @kelleyandcarlsadventures
properties.recommendation_summary: A Channel Islands mini guide — California's least-visited national park, an hour from LA: five islands by ferry from Ventura or Oxnard, with dolphins and whales en route. They did Anacapa and Santa Cruz over two days (the year-round ferries) and recommend both: on Santa Cruz, a sea cave kayaking tour, the 5.2-mile Potato Harbor Trail and island foxes by the campground; on Anacapa, Inspiration Point via the 2.5-mile East Anacapa Island Trail — with a May-July warning for the 10,000 nesting gulls. One new pin (Inspiration Point); the post is attached to the park, Potato Harbor and Santa Cruz pins.

Two new pins (Long Point, Kaymoor Miners); the post is attached to the Endless Wall, park and bridge pins.

properties.creator: @kelleyandcarlsadventures
properties.recommendation_summary: Katmai, 'the national park for bear lovers': brown bears crowd Brooks Falls for the salmon run every summer. Their tips — fly to King Salmon, then float plane or water taxi to Brooks Camp (or day-tour from Anchorage, King Salmon, Homer or Seward); camping permits drop in January/February and the lodge books by lottery ~1.5 years out; best late June-September (July peak); 1-3 days; must-sees Brooks Falls and the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes; and yes, bear school is mandatory. Attached as a source on all three pins.

properties.name: Lake Superior winter bucket list
properties.title: Lake Superior winter bucket list
properties.creator: @maddymarq
properties.recommendation_summary: Her personal Lake Superior winter bucket list — three things she plans every year: (1) sunrise at Artist Point in Grand Marais, Minnesota, over the frozen lake at 20 below zero or colder; (2) the Apostle Islands ice caves — kayak the mainland sea caves in summer, or walk across the frozen lake when the Park Service opens foot access; (3) Michigan's Keweenaw Peninsula for skiing, frozen waterfalls and sauna. All three are new pins (places identified from the reel's narration; the caption itself names no places).

properties.title: 57 parks down — our favorite parks, by category

properties.theme: Favorite national parks by category (57 parks visited)

Newspaper Rock petroglyphs — Bears Ears
properties.title: Newspaper Rock petroglyphs — Bears Ears
properties.creator: @christiandelatorre_
properties.recommendation_summary: Christian de la Torre at Newspaper Rock, Utah — panning shots of the famous petroglyph panel in Indian Creek Canyon (Bears Ears National Monument): 650+ carvings (figures, animals, footprints, handprints, spirals) spanning ~2,000 years, viewed from behind a railing at a roadside pullout on UT-211. 'I just can't get over these petroglyphs — history is so fascinating.' One new pin.

properties.name: Battery Spencer — best Golden Gate view
properties.title: Battery Spencer — best Golden Gate view
properties.creator: @thisworldofadventure
properties.theme: Battery Spencer / Golden Gate Bridge viewpoint
properties.recommendation_summary: Courtney & Matt's bucket-list Golden Gate viewpoint: Battery Spencer, the historic gun battery high above the bridge on the Marin Headlands (Sausalito side). Quick stop, huge payoff — views of the bridge, San Francisco and the bay. Go about an hour before sunset and stay through it; the colors keep improving. Fog can roll in fast and wipe the view. One new pin.

properties.name: God's Thumb via the Knoll — Lincoln City
properties.title: God's Thumb via the Knoll — Lincoln City
properties.creator: @littleredtravels
properties.recommendation_summary: Emily's (@littleredtravels) hike guide to God's Thumb via the Knoll Trail, Lincoln City, Oregon: 4 miles, 987 ft gain, 600 ft of it in the first mile ('a staircase to heaven'), through The Knoll meadow to the basalt headland above the Pacific. Dog friendly, no restrooms, street parking; don't take the cul-de-sac trail — the trail starts on the left. One new pin.

properties.creator: @se.kwon
properties.theme: Chicago first — self-cleaning public toilet at the Polish Triangle
properties.recommendation_summary: A tour of Chicago's first self-cleaning public toilet — the new JCDecaux automated restroom at the Polish Triangle in Wicker Park/West Town, opened Nov 11, 2026: free, ADA-compliant, 15-minute limit, and the bowl self-disinfects with high-pressure jets between uses.

properties.name: 3 BEST SPOTS FOR SUNSET IN DOOR COUNTY
properties.title: 3 BEST SPOTS FOR SUNSET IN DOOR COUNTY
properties.creator: @officetooutdoorsblog
properties.recommendation_summary: Three sunset spots in Door County, Wisconsin, ranked: Ellison Bluff County Park in Ellison Bay (cliffside overlook above Green Bay), Sunset Beach Park in Fish Creek (sun straight into the bay from a rocky shore and grassy bluff), and Pebble Beach in Sister Bay (a quiet, secluded pebble shoreline).

properties.name: Experience one of Acadia's hidden gems!
properties.title: Experience one of Acadia's hidden gems!
properties.creator: @ryan.goes.hiking

properties.name: Indiana World War Memorial, Indianapolis
properties.title: Indiana World War Memorial, Indianapolis
properties.creator: @englishman_in_indiana
properties.recommendation_summary: The Indiana World War Memorial in downtown Indianapolis — a 210-foot neoclassical monument of Indiana limestone modelled on the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, with a museum and atrium inside — and the 100-foot Veterans Memorial Obelisk opposite it, rising from a pink marble fountain with four bronze sculptures for law, science, religion and education.

properties.best_for: National park guide
properties.recommendation: A full park guide: best time to visit is July–September. Sights include Lake Clark itself, Proenneke Cabin at Twin Lakes, Turquoise Lake, Port Alsworth, Chinitna Bay, Crescent Lake, Redoubt and Iliamna volcanoes, and Telaquana Lake; top hikes are Beaver Pond Loop (3.5 mi easy), Teetering Rock (1.8), Tanalian Falls (4.3), Kontrashibuna Lake (4.3) and Tanalian Mountain (9.6 hard). The guide's key tip: the park has no road access — arrive by air taxi or floatplane from Anchorage or Homer, and build in buffer days because pass weather can ground bush planes.
properties.creator: @funsizewanderer

properties.best_for: National park / Their favorite way to visit Katmai
properties.recommendation: Kelley & Carl's favorite way to visit Katmai: reserve Brooks Camp camping permits in January/February on recreation.gov, fly Alaska Airlines from Anchorage to King Salmon, then float plane with Katmai Air to Brooks Camp. Day trips work too, but the viewing platforms get crowded for hours at midday — camping lets you watch the bears in the quiet hours. July is the classic month.
properties.creator: @kelleyandcarlsadventures
properties.reel_title: How to visit Katmai for the bears

properties.best_for: National park / 'For all the bear lovers'
properties.recommendation: Kelley & Carl's Katmai guide: every summer brown bears congregate at Brooks Falls for the salmon run — 'unlike any other wildlife viewing experience we've ever had.' Getting there: commercial flight to King Salmon, then float plane or water taxi to Brooks Camp (or day tours from Anchorage, King Salmon, Homer or Seward). Camping permits release in January/February; the lodge runs on a lottery about 1.5 years out. Best late June through September, July best of all; allow 1-3 days; and everyone goes to 'bear school' on arrival.
properties.creator: @kelleyandcarlsadventures
properties.reel_title: Katmai — the national park for bear lovers

properties.best_for: National park / The Dry Tortugas planning reel — ferry costs and warnings
properties.recommendation: Their Dry Tortugas planning reel: the most remote national park on the East Coast, 70 miles off the coast of Key West, reached only by seaplane or boat. They took the ferry — tickets were $235 per person and must be booked at least a few months in advance as they sell out quickly; the 2.5-hour ride can be rough and is not recommended if you are prone to seasickness. On the island: explore Fort Jefferson, the largest brick masonry structure in the Western Hemisphere, walk the moat, and snorkel the abundant marine life and coral reefs (equipment included with the ticket). Pack an extra pair of dry clothes for the return trip.

properties.best_for: Wildlife / Moose, elk and marmots — where and how to spot them
properties.recommendation: Their Rocky Mountain wildlife report: over two July days they saw a moose, many elk and a few marmots (bighorn sheep eluded them), all photographed from a safe distance with a 70–200mm lens. Most sightings came on the park's western side between the Alpine Visitor Center and Grand Lake, in the early afternoon to early evening — and never approach or feed wildlife.

properties.best_for: Park guide / Their exact 3-day mini guide itinerary
properties.recommendation: Their Rocky Mountain mini guide: Day 1 arrive via Denver, Lookout Mountain, the Peak to Peak Highway (Saint Catherine's Chapel on the Rock and Lily Lake), dinner and a stay in Estes Park. Day 2 the Bear Lake corridor lakes chain, Sprague Lake, Trail Ridge Road's overlooks and the Alpine Ridge Trail. Day 3 a strenuous hike (Sky Pond or Chasm Lake), Moraine Park, and the wildlife-rich western side to Grand Lake. Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road passes at 5 AM both days; Lookout Mountain, the chapel, Lily Lake and Moraine Park are named in the post but unpinned.
properties.creator: @kelleyandcarlsadventures
properties.reel_title: Rocky Mountain National Park mini guide — our 3-day itinerary

properties.best_for: Park guide / Top tips — start early, go on weekdays, respect the altitude
properties.recommendation: Their Rocky Mountain top tips from park #17: start as early as possible (Bear Lake corridor lots fill by 5:30 AM on summer weekends; there is a shuttle), visit on weekdays, drive Trail Ridge Road in summer, plan around the timed-entry reservation system, take altitude sickness seriously, bring bug spray and sun protection — and do not limit yourself to one area: the Bear Lake corridor, Trail Ridge Road and the quieter, wildlife-rich western side are all favorites.
properties.creator: @kelleyandcarlsadventures
properties.reel_title: Rocky Mountain landscapes are unreal — our top tips

properties.best_for: Park guide / Rocky Mountain planning guide — timed entry, lodging, timing
properties.recommendation: Their Rocky Mountain planning guide: stay in Estes Park or Grand Lake (Boulder and Loveland are about an hour away, Denver 1.5 hours), start as early as possible, summer is best because Trail Ridge Road is open (but it is also the busiest), allow 3+ days, take altitude sickness seriously, and never approach wildlife — they generally saw more on the quieter western side. The video adds the reservation mechanics: Timed Entry via recreation.gov (choose the 'Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road' option for full access), extra tickets released the night before at 7 PM MT, and Bear Lake corridor parking filling by 5:30 AM on a summer Saturday — use the shuttle.
properties.creator: @kelleyandcarlsadventures
properties.reel_title: This park is an adventurer's dream — Rocky Mountain planning guide

properties.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #1: caves carved into Navajo sandstone in the 1970s to harvest sand for glassmaking — now a free, photogenic scramble right off Highway 89, about 1.2 miles round trip with parking by the highway. Her caution: the scramble up can get a little scary; don't be afraid to turn back.
properties.creator: @giselle.on.trails

properties.best_for: Waterfall
properties.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #3: no hiking required if you have a 4x4 (don't attempt it in a normal car) — a 5.3-mile dirt road, about 45 minutes, to falls that pour over two pour-offs on La Verkin Creek: a cascade section and a clean 20-foot drop into a pool. Free BLM land, and the swimming is incredible in summer.
properties.creator: @giselle.on.trails
properties.reel_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

properties.best_for: Waterfall

Permits sell out 1–2 weeks ahead in summer, so book early — and rent the waders unless you want numb feet for an hour afterwards.
properties.creator: @giselle.on.trails
properties.reel_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

properties.best_for: Viewpoint / Their verdict — skip sunrise, go daytime or sunset
properties.recommendation: Their Horseshoe Bend verdict: 'THIS MAY BE CONTROVERSIAL BUT DON'T GO TO HORSESHOE BEND AT SUNRISE' — the surrounding area lights up beautifully, but the canyon itself stays dark and shadowed, the wait for the light is long, and the viewpoint is crowded and overwhelming even then. They left and returned later the same day in full sun, when the bend was beautiful. Their recommendation: visit during the day or at sunset. The walk is an easy 1.5 miles round trip, and parking costs $10 regardless of an America the Beautiful Pass (they misspoke '$20' in the video and corrected it in the caption and comments). Worth visiting — just not their favorite stop of the road trip.
properties.creator: @kelleyandcarlsadventures
properties.reel_title: Is Horseshoe Bend worth it? — skip sunrise

Their tips: pack plenty of water (few places to filter), no backpacking on the peak itself, and Thornton Lakes backpacking is by competitive NPS permit.

properties.best_for: Scenic drive
properties.recommendation: American Travel Archives' 'you will NOT believe this road' drive: the Million Dollar Highway (US-550) from Ouray to Silverton — 25 miles through the San Juan Mountains famous for steep cliffs, tight switchbacks and few guardrails. Stop at Red Mountain Pass for the classic overlook; autumn is the best time, when golden aspens contrast with the red and gray rock. Their tips: drive it in good morning light, take your time at the pull-offs, and think twice in an RV. Ouray and Silverton bookend it with hot springs and silver-mining history.
properties.creator: @americantravelarchives

properties.best_for: Stargazing
properties.recommendation: Jess drove 9 hours to camp on the Alvord Desert playa — under some of the darkest skies in Oregon — to teach herself astrophotography. She timed the trip under an almost-full moon by accident, so she waited for moonset, set a 3:24 AM alarm, and manually shot 105 long exposures (her old Sony has no intervalometer) to stitch a four-second starlapse. Her verdict: the Alvord had been on her list a long time and was worth every bit of the drive.

properties.best_for: Hike
properties.recommendation: WTA calls Mount Si the most popular hike in Washington — upwards of 100,000 hikers a year. The switchbacks start right at the trailhead; a mile and a half up you pass through Snag Flat, old-growth trees that survived fire and logging, then past a talus slope to the base of the Haystack, the true summit. 8.0 miles round trip with 3,150 ft of gain. Climbers training for Rainier haul heavy packs up here — the rule of thumb is that if you can make the top in under two hours, you're ready. A Discover Pass is required to park, and the lot fills early.
properties.creator: @outdoorsapp
properties.reel_title: Mount Si — Washington's most popular hike

properties.recommendation: The Needles Highway through Custer State Park winds between towering granite spires until the road tightens and passes through the Needles Eye Tunnel — a one-lane tunnel hand-carved through solid granite in the 1920s, one of the most photographed drives in the Black Hills. Know before you go: the tunnel is about 8'4" wide and 12' tall, one vehicle at a time, and RVs/trailers should avoid the route; drive it early morning or late afternoon for fewer cars and better light, and watch for bison, pronghorn and prairie dogs nearby.

properties.best_for: Fossils · A building built around a wall of dinosaur bones
properties.recommendation: About 30 minutes east of Vernal, a shuttle takes you to the Quarry Exhibit Hall — a building constructed around the sloped rock face where a 'log jam' of dinosaur bones was found in 1909. Hundreds of thousands of bones were excavated for museums around the world, but the rest were left in place, so you can see — and touch — real fossils where they were buried. You can shuttle back or hike back down for more fossils in the rock formations. The monument spans Utah and Colorado; the quarry is on the Utah side, and the creators wished they'd had time for more trails and a Green River float.
properties.creator: @the_vg_odyssey
properties.reel_title: Finding, seeing, touching dinosaur fossils at Dinosaur National Monument

properties.best_for: Spring swimming · Kayak a crystal-clear 72°F river
properties.recommendation: One of the oldest and most beautiful spring-fed rivers in Florida: crystal-clear water at 72°F year-round, surrounded by lush greenery that feels like a tropical jungle. It's Florida's 4th-largest spring; the headspring area was a privately owned theme park in the 1930s. Kayak, paddleboard, swim in the designated area, or walk the garden trails to see waterfalls — real ones, in Florida. Open daily 8 AM to sunset, $2 entry (tubing and kayak rentals extra). Pro tip from the reel: come early morning or late afternoon to beat the crowds, and bring your own snorkel gear to spot fish and turtles.
properties.creator: @americantravelarchives
properties.reel_title: Rainbow Springs — Florida's crystal-clear spring river

properties.best_for: Waterfall / Hike · Tallest waterfall between the Rockies and Appalachians

The journey is part of it: a steep, rugged hike drops nearly 1,400 feet into the hollow, and you climb every bit of it back out. Key catch from the reel: it's rain-fed, so it can be a powerful cascade after significant rainfall or barely a trickle in dry periods — go after rain (late winter through spring is peak flow).

properties.best_for: Hike · Towering rock pinnacles and fossil hunting
properties.recommendation: One of the most unique places in Missouri: a privately owned park north of Columbia (850 E. Pinnacles Rd, Sturgeon) that's open for public day use and feels like a rugged hike out west. Lower trails run along the creek to a shelter bluff for all ages; the real adventure is crossing the creek and taking the narrow, rocky path over the top of the towering rock formations. The spot is full of fossils — look in the creek and across the rocks for thousands of crinoids. Free (donation box at the kiosk); vault restroom; no alcohol, glass or drones. The reel's warnings: the upper ledge trails are not for young kids or anyone afraid of heights, don't cross the creek when the water is high, and expect wet feet even in summer.

Monadnock in southern New Hampshire — the 3,165-ft peak that gave 'monadnock' its name (an isolated mountain rising from the plain), reputed to be one of the most-climbed mountains in the world. The classic route is the White Dot Trail up from the state park headquarters (3.4–3.6 mi round trip, ~1,750 ft gain, with rock scrambles and stone steps) and down the White Cross — the bare, rocky summit opens to sweeping views across southern New Hampshire and, on clear days, all six New England states. A National Natural Landmark with a literary streak: Emerson and Thoreau both climbed and wrote about it. No dogs allowed on the mountain.

The reel's practical card: the Devil's Fork Trail is ~4 mi round trip with 13 unbridged crossings (or a 7-mi no-crossing route), budget 3–5 hours and 3 PM as the last start; don't go if the water is above your knees — the holler flash floods; free lot at 312 High Knob SC, Dungannon VA (no roadside parking — towed); go weekdays or early. Swimming season is over by fall — the hike is the experience then.

properties.best_for: Beach / Viewpoint · Golden Gate views without the crowds
properties.recommendation: San Francisco's most underrated Golden Gate view — and you'll probably have it to yourself. The family's route: park at the Langdon Court lot (free, mostly empty around 10 AM), walk toward Battery West, then take the Batteries to Bluffs Trail down to the beach (~0.5 mile, stairs involved — their 4- and 5-year-olds handled it fine), turn right toward Marshall's Beach and down a few more stairs. They stayed almost an hour without seeing another person. Safety notes from the reel: don't go at high tide — the beach becomes mostly inaccessible and dangerous, so check tides first; no restrooms or facilities; and it's a clothing-optional beach, worth knowing if you're bringing kids.

properties.reel_title: Marshall's Beach — San Francisco's most underrated Golden Gate view

properties.best_for: Swimming / Snorkel & dive · Underground spring inside a dry cave
properties.recommendation: Episode 1 of Jete's American Bucket List: Devil's Den in Williston, Florida (5390 NE 180th Ave) — you can swim inside the earth. It's an underground spring in a dry cave, over 100 feet across, reached only by descending a staircase into the sinkhole; it got its name because people once saw 'smoke' (winter steam) rising from the hole and thought it was where the devil lives. The water is 72°F year-round and you can snorkel or scuba dive — the reel's headline price was $30. Animal fossils from millions of years ago (Pleistocene finds, now at the UF Museum of Natural History) have been found down there.
properties.creator: @showmelovejete
properties.reel_title: Devil's Den, Florida — swim inside the earth for $30 (American Bucket List ep. 1)

properties.best_for: Scenic train / Canyon views · 1,000-ft gorge from an open-air car
properties.recommendation: Insane canyon views without hiking or driving sketchy roads: the Royal Gorge Route Railroad out of Cañon City, Colorado (~1 hr from Colorado Springs). The train runs the Arkansas River through a 1,000+ ft deep canyon with sheer granite cliffs on both sides, passing under the famous Royal Gorge Bridge — bald eagles, rafters, and dramatic rock formations along the route, with the best photo ops from the open-air car. Know before you go, per the reel: the ride is about 2 hours roundtrip and slow by design (scenery, not speed); parking is easy near the depot; there's a full kitchen and bar on most departures; and you can pair it with Royal Gorge Bridge Park if you have extra time.
properties.creator: @mccrawsonthemap
properties.reel_title: Royal Gorge Route Railroad — insane canyon views, no hiking required

properties.best_for: Summit hike / Sunset · Steep alpine climb to a 6,214-ft summit
properties.recommendation: Sunset on Vesper Peak — one of the most rewarding hikes off Washington's Mountain Loop Highway. The reel's card: about 6.5 miles round trip with 4,120 ft of gain; plan 6–8 hours (their hike took 5h40, and it runs longer than it looks — preparation is key, carry the 10 essentials). The trail starts in forest with steady switchbacks, then opens to alpine meadows, rocky slopes and big views; Vesper Lake near the top is a beautiful break spot (filter any water); the last stretch is steep and rocky. Sunset tip: start early enough to be at the summit before golden hour and bring a headlamp for the hike down. Pack layers, extra water, and traction in early season (snow can linger into summer); a Northwest Forest Pass is needed at the trailhead.

properties.recommendation: Don't miss this hidden gem: the Green River Gorge Resort property near Enumclaw, WA. The resort dates to the 1920s, when it operated as a privately owned getaway with a hotel and cabins; by the 1970s and '80s it had become a well-known local party spot. The resort itself no longer operates, but the property and trails are still accessible — check out the bridge, walk behind a waterfall into a hidden cave, and explore the area's unique rock formations. The reel's practical notes: $5 for parking, paid at a cash box; no restrooms; and the trail can be slippery, so watch your step. Leave no trace.

properties.best_for: Stay / Unique stay · Sleep inside a living cave in the Ozarks
properties.recommendation: Would you stay the night in this cave? Buried in the Ozark Mountains, Beckham Creek Cave Lodge (@beckhamcave) in Parthenon, Arkansas was once a private Cold War fallout shelter and has since been converted into one of the most beautiful and unique homes in the world. The 5,800 sq ft cave has 4 bedrooms, each with its own bathroom, and comfortably sleeps up to 12 guests — for less than $300 a person per night with a group. It was featured on Netflix's “World's Most Amazing Vacation Rentals,” and they offer cave tours you can take without staying the night.
properties.creator: @wanderlusttravelcouple
properties.reel_title: Would you stay the night in this cave? Beckham Creek Cave Lodge

properties.best_for: Waterfall / 66-foot waterfall at the end of a creekside climb
properties.recommendation: One of the best hikes in Virginia, and the waterfall is incredible: Cascades Falls in Pembroke, Virginia — she hiked it with her 8-year-old. It's 2 miles out and 2 miles back plus lots of elevation gain — a hard hike for beginners, but doable with kids (not recommended for kids under 6). About 4 hours from northern Virginia and 3 hours from Richmond. Her tips for solo moms and solo adventurers: bring way more water than you think you'll need and be prepared to take many breaks. (The falls themselves are a 66-foot cascade on Little Stony Creek, reached by the Cascades National Recreation Trail — US Forest Service.)
properties.creator: @shedarestogo
properties.reel_title: Cascades Falls, Pembroke Virginia — one of the best hikes in Virginia

properties.recommendation: Their White Sands guide: the dunes are not sand but gypsum — the largest gypsum dunes in the world. Best time to visit is fall through spring; plan one full day; park hours are 7 AM to sunset and the gate is closed outside them; bring lots of water, snacks and sun protection; nearby missile testing sometimes closes the park. For photos, start as early as possible and end with sunset — and go sand sledding (disc and wax from the visitor center).

Must-see stops: Many Parks Curve, Rainbow Curve, Forest Canyon, Rock Cut, Lava Cliffs, Gore Range, the Alpine Visitor Center and Medicine Bow Curve (named in the post but unpinned). Expect steep drop-offs without guardrails at times — and plenty of wildlife along the way.

properties.best_for: Hiking / Hidden sandstone arch in Sterling Canyon
properties.recommendation: Lily & Bryan call this hidden arch possibly the best hike in Sedona — it 'completely blew them away' and there were no crowds (their on-screen text jokes it 'ruined all other Arizona hikes'). The Vultee Arch Trail is 3.5 miles round trip with 547 ft of elevation gain through Sterling Canyon to the big natural arch, but the trailhead at the end of the rugged Dry Creek / Vultee Arch Road (Forest Road 152) strictly requires a 4x4 high-clearance vehicle.

properties.best_for: Waterfall / Nearly 200-foot falls reached by a chain-and-ladder cliff descent
properties.recommendation: Episode 5 of Cassie Compton's (@lafftravel) 'hikes to do before your knees give out': Mooney Falls drops nearly 200 feet into the most ridiculously blue water she's ever seen — but reaching the base means climbing down a cliff on chains, ladders and footholds carved into the rock. It's part of the Havasupai backpacking trip (10 miles in with a 35-pound pack on her first-ever backpacking trip; she lost three toenails and would do it all again in a heartbeat). A Havasupai reservation and permit are required, and the descent is steep and slippery — definitely not for everyone, but unforgettable if you're comfortable with heights.
properties.creator: @lafftravel
properties.reel_title: Hikes to do before your knees give out — Ep. 5: Mooney Falls

properties.best_for: Waterfall / The hike that 'ruined all other hikes'
properties.recommendation: 'Unfortunately this hike ruined all other hikes for me…' Mooney Falls at the Havasupai Reservation, just past the campground down a side canyon of the Grand Canyon. A $455 backpacking permit is required (they sell out fast, months in advance), and to reach the bottom you climb down chains and ladders on the cliff face.
properties.creator: @stumblinguponserendipity
properties.reel_title: Mooney Falls — the hike that ruined all other hikes

properties.best_for: Viewpoint / The optical-illusion viewpoint — coordinates published in the post
properties.recommendation: The secret behind the famous photo: only the Temple of the Moon is in the background — the Temple of the Sun is not even visible from this spot. The two 'matching' foreground monoliths are significantly smaller and only look comparable because they are closer. They publish the viewpoint's coordinates in the post: 38.4418188, -111.1952917. To reach it: follow the path by the little parking area on Cathedral Road, turn left, go behind the two smaller monoliths and climb the small hill. High-clearance 4WD required — the drive took them over an hour.
properties.creator: @kelleyandcarlsadventures
properties.reel_title: This hidden gem is an optical illusion — Temple of the Sun & Moon viewpoint

properties.recommendation: Their cherry-blossom planning guide: peak bloom around the Tidal Basin was expected March 23–26, 2024 per the National Park Service, with the full bloom period lasting up to 14 days. From their own peak-bloom Sunday visit the year before: go as early in the morning as possible and on a weekday — they arrived shortly after sunrise and it was manageable for 1–2 hours, but by 9–10 am 'everywhere was packed'; parking near the basin is very limited, so arrive super early or take public transportation. properties.best_for: Petroglyphs / One of the largest petroglyph panels in the US
properties.recommendation: 'I just CAN'T get over these petroglyphs!' Christian films the Newspaper Rock panel — a desert-varnish Wingate sandstone face in Indian Creek Canyon (Bears Ears) covered with 650+ carvings: human figures, deer, bighorn sheep, birds, footprints, handprints and spirals, etched over roughly 2,000 years by Archaic, Basketmaker, Fremont and Pueblo peoples. It's a short walk from the paved pullout on UT-211; you view the panel from behind a railing. 'History is so fascinating to me — I just want to learn more and more.'

properties.best_for: Viewpoint / Best Golden Gate Bridge view, especially at sunset
properties.recommendation: 'Add this to your bucket list — if you're looking for one of the best views of the Golden Gate Bridge, this is it.' The historic battery sits high above the bridge on the Marin Headlands, with an unreal view of the Golden Gate, San Francisco and the bay — a quick stop with a huge payoff, and one of their favorite viewpoints in the area. Their timing: arrive about an hour before sunset and stay as the sun goes down; the colors just keep getting better. Caveat: the famous San Francisco fog can roll in quickly, so the view can look completely different depending on when you visit.
properties.creator: @thisworldofadventure

properties.best_for: Hike / Coastal headland viewpoint over the Pacific
properties.recommendation: Emily's hike info for The Thumb via the Knoll Trail in Lincoln City: 4 miles with 987 ft of elevation gain — you'll gain 600 ft in the first mile, 'like climbing a staircase to heaven,' but the steep incline is worth it when you reach the top and see how The Thumb (a grass-topped basalt headland over the Pacific) gets its name. The route passes The Knoll meadow viewpoint on Lincoln City open space before the user-made path out to the Thumb. Practical notes from her caption: dog friendly, no restrooms, street parking that can get backed up — and IMPORTANT: do not take the trail at the end of the cul-de-sac; the trail begins on the left side.
properties.creator: @littleredtravels
properties.reel_title: God's Thumb via the Knoll — Lincoln City

properties.best_for: Landmark / Chicago's first self-cleaning public toilet
properties.recommendation: Chicago's first standalone automated public restroom — a JCDecaux kiosk in the Polish Triangle at Milwaukee, Ashland and Division, above the Division Blue Line station, which opened with a ceremonial 'First Flush' on the day this reel was posted (installation had wrapped Oct 23). Kwon tours it: free to use, spacious and ADA-compliant, with a 15-minute limit, an exit button plus a low foot-tap emergency button, and a combined sink/hand-dryer. After each use the toilet retracts into a side compartment where high-pressure jets wash and disinfect it (about a 30-second cycle), so the seat and paper can be slightly moist — she still calls it probably the nicest public bathroom she has ever used.
properties.creator: @se.kwon

properties.best_for: Landmark / 210-ft neoclassical memorial modelled on the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
properties.recommendation: One of America's most impressive war memorials, in downtown Indianapolis — a 210-foot neoclassical monument of Indiana limestone, modelled on the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Built to honor Hoosiers who served in the First World War and now commemorating all who served, with a museum and a spectacular atrium inside; above the entrance, 'To vindicate the principles of peace and justice in the world.'
